summary: The study describes the use of noncovalent DNA functionalization of single-walled carbon nanotubes (SWNTs) to enable uniform and conformal atomic layer deposition (ALD) of high-k dielectrics, specifically HfO2, down to a thickness of 2-3 nm. This approach allows for achieving a subthreshold swing (S) of 60 mV/decade at room temperature, which is the theoretical limit for low-power nanotube field-effect transistors (FETs).
